stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
stories.summary: The inflows come largely from the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams after heavy rain in NTR district
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Heavy rain continues in the Krishna basin under the influence of Cyclone Murasu.
The Water Resources Department (WRD) has suspended water supply to canals and opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage to send the surplus flow downstream.
The Prakasam Barrage was receiving 71,000 cusecs at 8 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), and the entire quantity was being released into the Krishna river towards the Bay of Bengal.
The water level stood at 12 feet.
To facilitate the discharge, 30 gates had been raised by two feet and another 40 by one foot.
WRD officials have stopped releases into the Krishna Eastern, Krishna Western and Guntur canals as a precaution against possible flooding.
The inflows are being fed largely by the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams, which drain into the Krishna from the local catchment areas.
Surplus releases from the barrage began on Tuesday night after inflows increased.
The decision to regulate the discharge comes amid reports of exceptionally heavy rainfall in NTR district and forecasts of more rain by the India Meteorological Department.
Officials are keeping a close watch on the river’s inflows and the situation in the upstream catchment areas.
Residents in low-lying settlements along the Krishna riverbanks have been asked to exercise caution and comply with instructions from the authorities.

Edlapadu in Palnadu district received the most rain in the State in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, 269.45 mm, according to the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES).

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh SEC reviews cyclone impact as MPTCs, ZPTCs go to polls today

article_sentences: With heavy rains and gales under the influence of Cyclone Murasu posing challenges in some parts of Andhra Pradesh, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha on Wednesday reviewed the arrangements for the MPTC and ZPTC elections scheduled for Thursday.
The SEC had elaborate discussions on the arrangements made for the polls with the District Collectors and Superintendents of Police.
The SEC sought reports on weather conditions, accessibility of polling stations, transport facilities and preparedness of poll personnel, particularly in the cyclone-hit districts.
The Collectors reportedly informed him that rainfall had subsided in most districts and that polling could be conducted without difficulty in all pockets, barring a few.

Mr. Punetha instructed the district administrations to continuously monitor local conditions and take preventive measures to ensure that voters and polling personnel did not face inconvenience in rain-affected areas.
He said decisions on any difficulties in conducting the elections would be taken based on detailed reports from field-level officials.
He directed officials of all departments to coordinate to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling, with adequate security arrangements to prevent untoward incidents.
State Election Secretary A. Mallikarjuna said around 2.52 lakh officials and employees had been drafted for election duties, while another 52,000 personnel would be engaged in the counting process.
Special attention was being paid to the arrangements in West Godavari, Guntur and Bapatla districts, which bore the brunt of the cyclone.
He stressed the need for videography at polling stations, including inside the premises wherever necessary, without compromising the secrecy of voting.
Any untoward incident should be recorded, he said, directing Presiding.
Officers to promptly alert Zonal Magistrates or the police in case of any malpractice or disturbance.

article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu has directed irrigation officials to remain on high alert in view of heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu and take immediate steps to drain rainwater stagnating in agricultural fields to prevent further damage to crops.

The Minister said heavy rainfall had been reported in Palnadu, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Krishna, Eluru and West Godavari districts.
The Nallamada and Parchur drains were flowing above their maximum levels in areas around Parchur, Bapatla, Chirala and Prattipadu.

Mr. Ramanaidu directed officials to ensure that rainwater accumulated in agricultural fields was drained immediately through canals and drains.
He also asked them to monitor field conditions continuously and ensure that farmers did not face difficulties.

The Minister said the Prakasam Barrage was receiving an inflow of 71,000 cusecs from streams in Guntur and Palnadu districts.
Water from the Budameru catchment was being diverted into the Krishna through the Budameru Diversion Canal, he added.
He called for continuous monitoring of inflows into the Prakasam Barrage and effective flood management.
Referring to the heavy rainfall in Vijayawada over the past two days, Mr. Ramanaidu said 3,000 cusecs of water was being diverted into the sea through the Enikepadu under-tunnel.

stories.headline: Supreme Court examines blanket immunity for CEC and Election Commissioners amid SIR hearing
stories.title: Supreme Court examines blanket immunity for CEC and Election Commissioners amid SIR hearing
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has sought responses on a plea challenging the immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act.
During a separate SIR hearing, the bench also questioned the Election Commission over voter exclusion, deadlines and safeguards in the electoral roll revision process.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court has issued notice on a public interest litigation challenging the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.

The provision grants the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners immunity from legal proceedings for acts performed or decisions taken in their official capacity during their tenure.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses on the petition filed by activist and lawyer Arun Kumar Agrawal.
The petitioner has argued that Section 16 provides blanket protection without specifying exceptions for actions allegedly carried out in bad faith or beyond the officials' legal authority.
The plea contends that such immunity limits citizens' access to civil and criminal remedies against members of the Election Commission.
The petition also argues that protecting the independence of the Election Commission should not mean removing accountability for its officials.
It has asked the court to declare Section 16 unconstitutional.
The development came during a separate hearing on petitions challenging the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
During the SIR hearing, the bench questioned the Election Commission about the urgency and implementation of the revision exercise.
It asked whether the process had been designed to harass or intimidate voters and questioned the need to conduct it in Delhi when no election was imminent.

stories.headline: “Public Office Not Consolation Prize For Defeated Politician”: Karnataka High Court Quashes Committee Headed By Congress Leader Who Lost Election
stories.title: “Public Office Not Consolation Prize For Defeated Politician”: Karnataka High Court Quashes Committee Headed By Congress Leader Who Lost Election
stories.summary: Desire to rehabilitate a leader who lost political ground can't justify creating an additional position, Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Desire to rehabilitate a leader who lost political ground can't justify creating an additional position, Court said.
The Karnataka High Court on Monday asked the state government to not treat a public office as a “consolation prize for a defeated politician” or a “reward for political loyalty.”

The Court made these stern remarks while setting aside the notifications through which K. Gopal Poojary— an Indian National Congress candidate who lost the 2023 state assembly elections from Byndoor constituency— was appointed as the chairman of the additional land regularisation committee.

“A personal request, political influence or the desire to rehabilitate a leader who has lost political ground cannot, by itself, furnish a justification for creating an additional position or arrangement.

The circumstances suggest an attempt to secure a position of authority through an indirect route and to regain power through a back-door route, rather than to address any genuine public necessity… The desire of an individual to cling on to power cannot be permitted to dictate the course of public administration,” the Bench of Justice D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan said.

“The State Government must, therefore, remain above considerations of personal political advancement and ensure that its decisions are guided by public interest and genuine administrative necessity, rather than by an attempt to accommodate an individual's desire to regain lost authority,” the Bench advised.

The present appeal before the Division Bench was filed by Gururaj Gantihole, an MLA from the Byndoor constituency and chairman of the regularisation committee for land grants as per Section 94-A(1) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act.
He challenged the Single Judge order which had dismissed his petition against two notifications.
The first notification, dated December 4, 2023, constituted an additional land regularisation committee and appointed Poojary as its chairman.

The second notification, dated December 26, 2023, allocated nearly twice as many pending applications (23,983 applications) to the Additional Committee compared to the appellant's committee (12,313 applications).
The appellant had also challenged the constitutional validity of Rule 108-EE of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966 in his petition.
Under the Act, an additional land regularisation committee can be formed if the government is of the opinion that constitution of an additional panel is necessary.

article_sentences: The Court held that the principle of 'equal pay for equal work' did not apply in the instant case.

The Supreme Court has upheld the constitutional validity of a regulation permitting the deduction of service pension from the salary payable to retired government servants appointed as Chairman or Members of the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (UKPSC), holding that the pension is merely kept in abeyance during their tenure and is restored thereafter.

A bench of Justice S.V.N. Bhatti and Justice N.V. Anjaria set aside the Uttarakhand High Court's 2010 judgment which had declared Regulation 7(2) of the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2004, unconstitutional for violating Article 14 read with Article 39(d) of the Constitution.
The High Court had held that deducting pension earned from previous government service from the salary payable for the constitutional post violated the principle of “equal pay for equal work.”

Disagreeing with the High Court, the Supreme Court held that the deduction did not amount to a withdrawal of the pensionary benefit, but only its temporary withholding during the period of service as Chairman or Member of the Commission.
“The question of breach of doctrine of equal pay for equal work does not arise,” the Court observed, adding that the High Court had misdirected itself in holding the regulation unconstitutional.
The Court also held that a Government servant cannot turn around to question the conditions after accepting them.

“…a Government servant or an employee, who accepts the post cannot afterwards be permitted to resile from or to agitate in respect of the service conditions and the service regulations attached to the post which he accepted.”, observed the bench.
The Respondent, having been superannuated from the Indian Army from the post of Lt. General in 2006, was appointed as Chairman of the State PSC.

Regulation 7(2) of the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2004 (“Regulation”), which was in force when the Respondent joined as Chairman, determines salary by applying the principle of “pay minus pension”.

This means the pension, which was entitled to be received by the Respondent upon retirement from the Indian Army, would be kept in abeyance till his current role as Chairman, and the salary for the Chairman post would exclude the pension amount.
In essence, upon appointment after retirement, the principle of “pay minus pension” was applied in determining the amount of salary.

The Chief Justice's own docket from that week shows the confusion at work.
Three days earlier, the Chief Justice's own bench had already entered the domain he later disclaimed.

On 9 October, a bench of the Chief Justice and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Police de-notified Jantar Mantar as a protest site, moving dissent to Ramlila Ground, Burari and East Delhi.
Prohibitory orders, detentions and the removal of a protest site are exactly the measures the Constitution asks courts to test for proportionality.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) questioned whether State High Courts have parens patriae (guardian) jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths while staying a Madras High Court order that constituted a Board of Management to administer the ancient Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu back to glory.

A Bench of Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi issued notice to the State of Tamil Nadu and froze the implementation of the October 30 High Court order, which said the Podhu Dikshidar (a hereditary community of priests) had maladministered the temple ever since its running was handed over to them following orders passed by the Supreme Court in 2014.
The High Court had appointed retired judges V. Bharathidasan and R. Suresh Kumar to chair the Board of Management (BoM).

Retired IAS officer C. Rajendran was designated its member, and the secretary of the Podhu Dikshidar’s association and the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department secretary would be the ex-officio members.

The BoM, in consultation with the Tamil Nadu Heritage Commission, was ordered to undertake the removal of unauthorised constructions put up on the temple premises that caused damage to the ancient structure.
The High Court Bench had tasked the BoM to take steps to retrieve the temple properties under encroachment with the help of the district administration.

Appearing for Tamil Nadu government, senior advocates Shekhar Naphade and Jaideep Gupta submitted that there was severe damage caused to the property and the Podhu Dikshidars had not shared the full accounts of the income derived from the temple in the last 12 years.
Mr. Naphade said the High Court had parens patriae jurisdiction over public temples to protect the interest of the presiding deity, considered as juristic person by law.
“Is this parens patriae only for temples or other places of worship?” Justice Kumar asked the State government.
Mr. Naphade responded that the law only recognised parens patriae jurisdiction for public temples, not churches or other places of worship of faiths.
Senior advocate Sai Deepak Iyer, for the opposite side, submitted that the court should look into why parens patriae doctrine applied to temples alone.
“Please, do not make any sweeping statements,” Justice Kumar said.

article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a scheme to promote critical mineral processing to encourage domestic value additional.

It also gave its nod to the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) for expeditious trial of cases of rape and under POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act for another five years.
The Cabinet gave its nod to the ‘capex support scheme to promote critical mineral processing’ with a financial outlay of ₹2,814 crore over a period of five years.
It has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for the establishment and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities.

According to an official statement, the scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain.
The scheme targets processing of Lithium and Nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds.
Cobalt is expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production.
This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, battery energy storage system (BESS), electronics, defence and speciality steel.

Under the scheme, capital subsidy of 30 per cent of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants, comprising two lithium processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 30 kt each) and two nickel processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 50 kt each).
The maximum capital support will be capped at ₹500 crore per lithium beneficiary and ₹900 crore per nickel beneficiary, respectively.
The selection of beneficiaries shall be carried out through a two-stage process.

In the first stage, applications shall be assessed for technical qualification, and only technically qualified applicants shall be eligible to participate in the second stage of financial bidding, the government noted.

stories.title: Supreme Court Rejects Plea To Rotate SC/ST Reservations Of Assembly & Parliament Seats, Affirms Validity Of S.9(1)(c) Delimitation Act

article_sentences: The Court declined interference, observing that it was a matter of legislative policy.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday rejected a plea seeking mandatory rotation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament, holding that the issue falls within the legislative domain of Parliament and cannot be directed by the courts.

The Court was dealing with a petition challenging Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, which requires reserved constituencies to be located in areas where the proportion of SC/ST population is comparatively large.
After the Allahabad High Court upheld Section 9(1)(c) and refused to order rotation of reserved seats, the petitioner approached the Supreme Court.

The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana refused to interfere with the High Court's judgment, observing that it was a matter for the legislature to decide.
The Court allowed the petitioner to file a representation before the elected representatives seeking a change in the law.

The petitioner, Jagdish Singh, an elector of the 191-Kadipur Assembly Constituency in Sultanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, had argued that the seat had remained reserved for SCs for nearly seven decades since its creation.

He contended that the continuous reservation without rotation violated Articles 14, 15 and 19 of the Constitution, diluted the right to vote by compelling voters to choose only from SC candidates, and benefited only a few families rather than the broader community.
He sought a system of rotation similar to that provided for panchayats and municipalities under Articles 243D and 243T.
During the hearing, the bench observed that voters in a multiparty democracy are expected to vote on the basis of political ideology rather than caste or religion.

Justice Bagchi noted that whether concentrating reserved seats in areas with larger SC/ST populations creates caste divisions is a matter for the legislature to examine and does not by itself render the law unconstitutional.

The Court distinguished the constitutional right to vote from any claimed right to contest from a particular constituency, pointing out that general-category candidates can contest from non-reserved seats.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 2,814 crore scheme to promote critical mineral processing
stories.title: Cabinet approves Rs 2,814 crore scheme to promote critical mineral processing
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 4: The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore over a period of five years. Processing of critical minerals remains geographically concentrated in a few global locations. This exposes supply chains to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility, and potential supply restrictions, posing severe threats to supply chain resilience and economic security. This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets. At present, India remains substantially dependent on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials, owing to the nascent stage of domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals, including Lithium, Nickel, Cobalt. Domestic processing capacity for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale projects facing challenges relating to high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials. Domestic processing capacity is therefore imperative for maximising value addition, achieving import substitution, and establishing resilient end-to-end value chains. Against this backdrop, the “Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing” has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for the establishment and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities. The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain. The scheme targets processing of Lithium and Nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), electronics, defence, speciality steel etc. The proposed scheme envisages a total financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore. The scheme period is from FY 2026-27 to 2030-31. Under the scheme, capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants, comprising two lithium processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 30 kt each) and two nickel processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 50 kt each). The maximum capital support will be capped at Rs.500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs.900 crore per nickel beneficiary, respectively. The selection of beneficiaries shall be carried out through a two-stage process. In the first stage, applications shall be assessed for technical qualification, and only technically qualified applicants shall be eligible to participate in the second stage of financial bidding. For each mineral, two beneficiaries shall be selected based on the least-cost criterion, i.e., the lowest CAPEX support sought by the bidders under the Scheme. The incentives will be disbursed in three tranches linked to the achievement of specified milestones. The Scheme is an important step towards advancing the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by supporting the development of resilient domestic processing infrastructure and strengthening India’s capabilities across the critical mineral value chain.

stories.headline: Cabinet clears Viksit Bharat Initiative (VISTAR) to strengthen statistical systems, analytics and research from 2026-27 to 2030-31
stories.title: Cabinet clears Viksit Bharat Initiative (VISTAR) to strengthen statistical systems, analytics and research from 2026-27 to 2030-31
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 04: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)’ Scheme for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs.4,371.10 crore. Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets. The VISTAR scheme will provide the strategic flexibility to dynamically allocate resources based on immediate policy needs, fostering a holistic approach to large-scale survey execution, methodological research, digital transformation, and national data governance. VISTAR Scheme will encompass all statistical and data management activities of MoSPI and it will play a crucial role for upgrading the official statistical system of the country. The three components of the VISTAR scheme are as follows: Component 1: Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem; Component 2: Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS); and Component 3: Economic Census (EC) Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, MoSPI proposes conducting 59 surveys during the 16th FC cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously, potentially filling up critical data gaps in various sectors, thereby, improving decision-making and enabling timely and targeted policy interventions. In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalization of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis. MoSPI is planning to release new metrices, including the Headline Index of Services Production, the Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. MoSPI will build upon the foundational pillars of data harmonisation such as data cataloguing, machine readability, interoperability, sharing protocols, and privacy by design etc. to dismantle silos and improve programme targeting, reduce duplication, and pave the way for AI-driven decision-making across government levels. By mainstreaming alternate sources—like mobile phone, scanner, and e-commerce data—MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking. Furthermore, MoSPI will ensure capacity building and enhanced opportunities for youth and researchers through Internship Scheme for students and research proposals from academic & research institutions. Under the Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS) component, funds are to be provided to State/UT Governments for transforming the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework (SSS 2.0). The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking. MoSPI will provide technical support to scale up generation of district-level estimates and million-plus city level estimates in flagship national surveys (e.g., PLFS, HCES, ASUSE) as well as in compilation of State/District level GDP and State level IIP. Under the Economic Census (EC) component, MoSPI will undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States / UTs which will provide granular data and activity details of all the non – farm establishments and workers hired, therein, upto Gram Panchayat and Ward level, providing an assessment of the unorganized sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions. The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave way for estimating the contribution of unorganized sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined to grant a one-time relaxation of the mandatory practice requirement for in-service court employees seeking entry into the judicial service, orally observing that judicial posts cannot be treated as a promotional avenue for other cadres.

A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana, dismissed applications filed by court staff who had approached the Court seeking modification of the Bhumika Trust judgment, which waived the practice condition for graduates till March 31, 2027.
The applicants, 21 officers from Karnataka sought relaxation for Court staff as well.

Senior Advocate Aditya Sondhi, appearing for the applicants, submitted that different States were applying the Court's earlier judgment in the Bhumika Trust case inconsistently with respect to in-service candidates.

He pointed out that Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Maharashtra continued to permit recruitment by transfer for in-service persons, while Karnataka insisted that such candidates must compete in the open category.

CJI Surya Kant responded that the creation of a separate channel was a matter for the States under Article 309 or through legislation, but the Court would not issue a direction to introduce another mode of recruitment.
“That is for the State.
They can exercise their power under Article 309, or perhaps through legislation.
But we would like to keep ourselves away from issuing a direction that they should introduce another channel of recruitment,” the Chief Justice said.
Sondhi argued that persons in service in Karnataka were being hit by the rules after the High Court, in exercise of its administrative powers, relied on the Supreme Court's judgment.
“I am willing to compete.
In Karnataka, until 2026, in-service candidates were permitted,” he submitted.

stories.headline: Iran exempts ships from India and 3 other nations from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz
stories.title: Iran exempts ships from India and 3 other nations from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Dubai, Nov 4: Iran has exempted commercial ships from four countries, including India and China, from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, a top Iranian official has said, amid continued attacks on vessels attempting to cross the strategic waterway. Amir Hayat Moghadam, Deputy Chairman of the Iranian Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, made the announcement in an interview with the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) on Tuesday. "We have currently exempted four countries - India, China, Iraq and Qatar - from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either," he was quoted as saying by the semi-official news agency. Moqaddam said the exemptions were based on specific considerations and mutual interests. He said that facilitating the passage of Indian ships was intended to allow imports of medicines from India, while the exemption for Chinese vessels was intended to secure Beijing's political support. The Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, handles roughly 20 per cent of global energy supplies in normal times. Shipping through the waterway has been severely disrupted since February 28, when the US and Israel launched joint attacks on Iran, triggering retaliatory strikes. Iran moved to shut the waterway soon after the US-Israeli bombing began, and Washington responded weeks later with a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iran, which has imposed strict restrictions on traffic, allows only a few vessels to pass through the waterway while others undergo screening and, in some cases, pay transit fees. At least 15 Indian seafarers have been killed in attacks on ships in the region since the conflict began in February. In the latest incident, an Indian sailor was killed in an attack on the commercial vessel MSV Al Jusufi near Limah in Oman on Monday evening. India, which has been consistently calling for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy, has termed the continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region as "deeply concerning". India has said that the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest.
